title: Report on every nested project with -r
lead: `list`, `check`, `status`, `stats` and `next` take `-r/--recursive`. With it, they find every slicer project at or below the start directory and run once in each project, reading only. The output is one result per project.
findings_note: owner request, session 2026-10-09; discover() only walks up, so a folder of repos needs one call per project
boundary: **Not in this slice:** `-r` on any command that changes state, ranking items across projects, a combined census, a config option for which directories to skip, and the TUI.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: `discover()` only walks up from the working directory to the first `.slicer/`. A monorepo or a folder of repos takes one call per project and a hand-kept list of paths. Reading every project from one call is cheap, and state stays in each checkout, so it fits the goals.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/store.py`: `discover_all(start) -> list[Path]`.
- `src/slicer/cli.py`: the `-r/--recursive` flag on `list`, `check`, `status`, `stats` and `next`, and the loop over projects.
- `src/slicer/errors.py`: the `no_project` code.
- `docs/commands.md`, `docs/agents.md` (the new JSON envelope), `CHANGELOG.md`.
- `tests/test_recursive.py`.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
The start directory is `--root`, or the working directory if none is given. `-r` never walks up.

`discover_all` walks down with `os.walk(followlinks=False)` and sorts directory names at each level. A directory is a project when it holds `.slicer/config.json`. The start directory is included when it is one. The walk skips dot-directories (which covers `.git`, `.slicer`, `.worktrees` and `.venv`), `node_modules`, and symlinked directories. It keeps descending inside a project it has found, so a project nested in a project is found too. Results are absolute paths sorted by POSIX path relative to the start directory, so output is deterministic.

Each found project runs the existing handler with `root` set to that project; do not copy the handlers. Collect the payload `_emit` would have printed for each project. `next -r` returns one next item per project and never ranks across projects, because scores are relative within one project.

Text output is a `== <relative path> ==` header (`.` for the start directory), then that project's normal text, with one blank line between projects.

JSON is `{"projects": [{"path": "<relative posix>", "exit": N, "result": {...}}]}`. A project that fails to load has `"error": {"code": ..., "message": ...}` in place of `result`. `--lean` applies inside each result.

The exit code is the highest any project returned: `check -r` exits 1 when any project drifts and 3 when any project is corrupt or locked. One failing project never stops the others. No project found exits 2 with code `no_project`.

`-r` with `next --start`, or with any other option that changes state, is a usage error (exit 2) and writes nothing. `-r` takes no lock.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: `python3 tests/affected.py --run`, then `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests`. `slicer check` passes. The recursive check, run from a directory above two fixture projects, reports both. `git diff --check` is clean.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: Branch `feature/s240-recursive` in `.worktrees/s240`. Do not commit, merge, or push until the owner asks. This repo finishes with `handoff`.
